drivingQuestion: From where is exemption derived for eaten portions and for non-concluding rites done outside?

segments.he: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״עוֹלָה״ – מָה עוֹלָה שֶׁהִיא רְאוּיָה לְהַעֲלָאָה, אַף כֹּל שֶׁרְאוּיָה לְהַעֲלָאָה.
segments.en: «The verse states» with regard to the prohibition against sacrificing outside the Temple courtyard: “Whatever man…that sacrifices «a burnt offering» or sacrifice, and brings it not to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, to sacrifice it to the Lord, that man shall be cut off from his people” (Leviticus 17:8–9). The term “burnt offering” teaches: «Just as a burnt offering is fit for offering up» upon the altar, «so too, anything that is fit for offering up» is included in the prohibition. All of the offerings listed in the baraita are not sacrificed upon the altar but given to the priests.

segments.he: מִנַּיִן שֶׁאַף הַיּוֹצֵק, וְהַבּוֹלֵל, וְהַפּוֹתֵת, וְהַמּוֹלֵחַ, וְהַמֵּנִיף, וְהַמַּגִּישׁ, וְהַמְסַדֵּר הַשֻּׁלְחָן, וְהַמֵּטִיב אֶת הַנֵּרוֹת, וְהַקּוֹמֵץ, וְהַמְקַבֵּל בַּחוּץ – שֶׁפָּטוּר?
segments.en: «From where» is it derived «that even» with regard to «one who pours» oil onto the meal offering, «and one who mixes» the oil into the flour of the meal offering, «and one who breaks» the loaves of the meal offering into pieces, «and one who salts» the meal offering or other offerings, «and one who waves» the meal offering, «and one who brings» the meal offering to the corner of an altar that he constructs outside the courtyard, «and one who arranges» the shewbread on «the table» outside the Sanctuary, «and one who removes the ashes» from «the lamps» of the Candelabrum, «and one who removes a handful» from a meal offering, «and one who collects the blood» of an offering in a vessel, if he did so «outside» the Temple courtyard he is «exempt.»

segments.he: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״אֲשֶׁר יַעֲלֶה עוֹלָה אוֹ זָבַח״ – מָה הַעֲלָאָה שֶׁהִיא גְּמַר עֲבוֹדָה, אַף כֹּל שֶׁהוּא גְּמַר עֲבוֹדָה.
segments.en: «The verse states: “That sacrifices a burnt offering or sacrifice”» (Leviticus 17:8). «Just as sacrificing is the conclusion of» the sacri-ficial «service, so too, any» rite «that is the conclusion of» a sacrificial «service» is included. All of these are excluded from the prohibition, as there are rites that follow them.
